title: if-else conditional statement
concept: Basic branch statement that executes different code depending on conditions

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
**`int main() {`** — The starting point of the program. When `main` is called, a **stack frame** is created on the stack.

In this lesson, you will learn how to branch the flow of a program based on a condition using a single `temperature` variable.

steps.title: Temperature variable initialization
steps.explanation: **`int temperature = 35;`** — Declare an integer variable `temperature` and initialize it to **35**. In this one line, 4 bytes of space are reserved within the stack frame, and `35` is stored in that space.

steps.title: evaluate if condition (true)
steps.explanation: **`if (temperature >= 30) {`** — This is where the **if statement** appears, the core of this lesson. If the condition inside the parentheses is **true (non-zero)**, the code inside the braces is executed, and if it is **false (0)**, it is skipped.

steps.title: Execute branch that is true (output)
steps.explanation:
**`printf("It's hot!\n");`** — Since the condition was true, this line is executed and prints `It's hot!` to the screen.

if-else The most important rule of the if-else chain is that if one condition is true, only that block is executed and the remaining `else if` and `else` are **all unconditional.

steps.title: else if / else skip
steps.explanation: **`} else if (temperature >= 20) {`** — Since the preceding `if` condition was already true, this `else if` and the `else` block below are **not even evaluated** and are skipped entirely. The conditional expression `temperature >= 20` is not executed.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation: **`return 0;`** — The conditional branch ends and the program terminates normally. `return 0` is a signal to the operating system that "finished without a problem", and as main's stack frame is released, `temperature` is also removed from memory.

quiz.explanation:
The if-else if chain is checked in order from the top, executing only the block whose condition is true the first time.
If temperature = 20, the first (>= 30) is false and the second (>= 20) is true, so only B is output.
The third (>= 10) is also true, but it is not executed because it has already been caught in the second.

misconceptions.wrong: else if conditions are also always checked
misconceptions.correct: If one of the preceding if or else if is true, all else if / else after it is skipped.
misconceptions.why: if-else If-else is connected in a 'chain', so when the first true block is found, the rest are ignored.

keyTakeaway: if-else An if-else chain checks conditions from the top, executing only the first block that is true.
